## 開篇固定收益論點

8月5日美國固定收益市場收盤，前兩個交易日的漲勢轉為高檔整理，並未反轉。2年期美國公債殖利率下跌2個基點至4.18%，5年期與10年期分別持平於4.33%及4.63%，30年期則下跌1個基點至5.17%。荷姆茲海峽朝暫時恢復通航取得進展，持續壓低近期能源通膨的尾端風險；但Fed官員愈來愈明確呼籲升息，加上實質殖利率居高，使這項利多未能連續第3個交易日進一步壓低曲線腹部殖利率。

收盤結構凸顯市場拉鋸。10年期損益兩平通膨率再降1個基點至2.22%，延續前兩個交易日油價重挫帶動的通膨重新定價；10年期實質殖利率則上升1個基點至2.41%，使名目殖利率持平。WTI下跌0.98%至$75.03，布蘭特原油持平於$79.36；與此同時，相關報導已從可能的除雷安排，推進至美國、伊朗與阿曼可能達成為期60天的航運協議。市場進一步移除短期能源溢價，卻未降低持有存續期間所要求的實質報酬。

Fed溝通是主要反向力量。明尼亞波利斯聯準銀行總裁Neel Kashkari表示，現在就應開始逐步升息，年底前升息3次仍在可能範圍內；後續路徑將取決於通膨是持平還是惡化。堪薩斯城聯準銀行總裁Jeff Schmid另指出，強勁需求與投資代表目前政策並不具限制性，並警告不應假定供給驅動的通膨升勢會自行消退。兩人之所以強調需求延續，是因為2026年美國AI投資估計接近$6,000億，相當於GDP的1.8%；即使油價下跌減輕整體通膨壓力，龐大投資動能仍為經濟帶來強勁推力。

美國財政部再融資聲明排除了眼前的供給衝擊，卻保留較長期的融資難題。附息債券與浮動利率票券發行規模預計至少未來數季維持不變；同時，財政部將未來發行「增加」改稱範圍較廣的「調整」。新措辭提高政策彈性，但本季借款預估已上調$680億至$7,390億。短期附息債券供給穩定，避免30年期債券遭遇賣壓；然而，融資依賴國庫券，加上借款需求上升仍無長久解方，使期限面的利多有限。

信用與全球市場也顯示，市場承接功能正常，但分化十分顯著。美國信用債基金幾乎持平；一筆為醫療保健收購案融資的$22億私人貸款正在推進，利差至少8個百分點；超大規模雲端業者持續大量發債，則壓抑科技公司債表現。海外方面，印度央行將政策利率維持在5.25%，並大幅壓低市場對10月升息的預期；菲律賓通膨仍達6.2%，泰國則放緩至1.95%。加彭取得IMF方案的前景改善，與塞內加爾的債務困境形成對比。共同的能源衝擊正在消退，但各地政策空間與融資條件，仍取決於本地通膨、財政可信度及資本結構。

## 美國公債利率、Fed定價、實質殖利率與曲線結構

美國公債殖利率曲線前端小幅走低，其餘券期變動不大。2年期殖利率下跌2個基點，幅度大於30年期的1個基點；5年期與10年期則持平。2s10s斜率擴大2個基點至45個基點，2s30s陡峭化1個基點至99個基點。這是由政策敏感券期帶動的小幅牛市趨陡，並非廣泛的存續期間漲勢。前一交易日5年期與10年期券殖利率領跌，且降幅較大，因此本日收盤是在較低殖利率水準附近整理。

一週比較顯示，利多雖具實質意義，但仍不完整。2年期、5年期及10年期殖利率一週均下跌4個基點，30年期則下跌3個基點。然而，與1個月前相比，曲線仍全面上移：2年期高4個基點、5年期高10個基點、10年期高14個基點、30年期高19個基點。油價反轉已修復最近一週的衝擊，但長端一個月以來更大幅度的上升，仍反映實質報酬居高、政策不確定性與財政供給。

通膨連結債定價顯示不同期間的分歧。10年期實質殖利率升至2.41%，損益兩平通膨率降至2.22%，因此10年期名目殖利率沒有變動。30年期實質殖利率為2.96%，當日持平，但較1個月前仍高17個基點。名目殖利率最新看似穩定，實際上掩蓋折現率進一步由預期通膨轉向實質利率。能源價格下跌降低近期發生第二輪衝擊的機率，卻未使投資人相信Fed反應函數已轉趨寬鬆，或長期資本報酬要求已經降低。

兩者分化也讓「損益兩平通膨率偏低即可化解通膨疑慮」的論點更難成立。Barclays與HSBC策略師指出，在損益兩平通膨率接近一年低點、30年期實質殖利率近期觸及2008年以來最高之際，長天期通膨連結債可用來防範Fed延後行動。這項看法著眼未來，並未推翻當日通膨補償下降的事實，而是凸顯風險不對稱：市場可以反映荷姆茲海峽的短期利多，同時仍願意支付避險成本，防範能源情勢反轉，或政策反應容許通膨延續。

相較前一交易日，Kashkari更明確點出近期政策挑戰。他主張利率應開始逐步上調，但對9月決策仍未確定，後續行動則取決於新公布數據。他表示年底前可能升息3次，擴大了利率路徑的可能分布，卻未提供各種情境的發生機率。Schmid的論點則不只著眼能源，而是認為強勁需求與投資構成收緊政策的理由，並警告需求穩健時，供給衝擊更容易推升通膨。

AI投資動能為需求論點提供量化依據。2026年全球AI資本支出估計約$1兆，其中美國略低於$6,000億。美國AI資本支出今年估計占GDP的1.8%，2027年升至2.5%，2028年再升至2.8%。這些估計並非同一交易日公布的活動數據，但足以說明為何油價路徑下移，不必然帶動實質殖利率同幅下降。即使外部通膨衝擊減弱，投資仍可支撐成長、融資需求及資源壓力。

債務管理在標售規模方面帶來眼前的安心訊號。美國財政部維持指引，表示名目附息債券與浮動利率票券的發行規模至少未來數季不變，符合市場原先預期，任何調整都將延至2027年較後期。下週規模$1,250億的再融資，預計籌得約$287億新資金。公告確立了時程與短期供給量；需求品質仍要由實際標售結果決定。

細微的措辭調整保留了另一項期限溢價問題。美國財政部目前表示，正在評估未來附息債券與浮動利率票券銷售的「調整」，而非「增加」；同時仍傾向在最終增發時偏重較短券期。美國財政部借款諮詢委員會（TBAC）表示，目前預估仍可能需要在10月1日起的會計年度提高附息債券發行量，並敦促採用保留彈性的措辭。面對$7,390億的本季借款預估，附息債券規模不變只會把更多融資轉向國庫券，並提高對未來短期利率衝擊的敏感度，並未消除融資需求。

利率市場的結論是，名目殖利率在兩股相反力量拉鋸下持穩。荷姆茲海峽進展與油價下跌持續壓低通膨補償，並帶動2年期債券上漲。Fed鷹派溝通、強勁投資需求及未解決的未來借款需求，使實質殖利率維持高檔，曲線腹部則持平。過去一週的債券跌勢已經逆轉，但長端殖利率一個月來的升勢尚未消退，後續曲線走向取決於實際國內數據及標售承接情況。

## 信用、融資與初級市場承接

美國公債大致持平之際，美國整體信用債價格變動有限。LQD下跌0.02%，HYG下跌0.04%，JNK下跌0.08%。這些變動不足以顯示信用風險遭到全面重新定價，基金報酬也無法判斷現券利差方向。較長天期公司債指數當日上漲約0.16%，接近20年期以上美國公債指數的0.20%漲幅。整體存續期間市場仍正常運作，個別發行人的融資條件則提供更有用的訊息。

私人信貸市場顯示，市場有能力承接大型收購融資，但成交成本偏高。Ares Management正主導一筆$22億直接貸款，支應MedImpact Holdings計畫收購總部位於波多黎各的Medical Card System。這筆貸款利率可能至少較基準高8個百分點。醫療保健業先前受到破紀錄贖回干擾；若交易以此條件完成，將顯示市場仍能承接大型交易，但利差已納入槓桿、流動性不足及執行風險的大幅補償。

這筆交易介於前一交易日所見的兩個極端之間。它既沒有AbbVie取得的龐大認購簿與投資級殖利率曲線融資管道，也不同於Baker Tilly的聯貸案；後者因貸款人要求提高利差，最終未能完成與贊助人股利相關的再融資。目前新增變化是，只要經濟條件足夠優厚，私人市場已再度具備收購融資能力。相較美國公債1至2個基點的變動，資金用途與貸款人補償仍更具決定性。

超大規模雲端業者發債帶來更廣泛的投資組合承接問題。美國投資級市場承擔了不成比例的AI基礎建設融資，既有債券因投資人為新供給騰出空間，並質疑資本支出報酬而走弱。Amazon上月發行$250億債券，促使投資人賣出已流通的超大規模雲端業者債券，以支應初級市場申購。7月Meta平均利差擴大約22個基點，Oracle擴大29個基點，顯示壓力直接集中在該產業，並非一般性的存續期間效應。

歐洲市場也正成為同一供給管道的一環。Alphabet首度發行英鎊與瑞士法郎債券，並發行歐元債；大型科技借款人若進一步分散融資幣別，可能削弱歐洲投資級債券的相對估值優勢。多數發行人資產負債表穩健，可限制近期償債疑慮；尚未解決的問題是，投資收益是否足以支撐持續借款。即使每家借款人都維持市場准入，且違約風險仍低，大量供給仍可能削弱次級市場表現。

這套機制把總體韌性與信用壓力連結起來。AI投資支撐美國需求，並使實質殖利率維持高檔；但相關融資迫使公司債投資組合騰出空間，也提高對單一資本支出主題的集中度。票息收入或可抵銷部分按市價計算的損失，但若初級市場反覆提供讓利，或投資人持續賣出舊券，將顯示邊際承接意願正在下降。關鍵區別不在資金是否存在，而在投資組合願以何種價格承接下一波科技業存續期間供給。

融資狀況並未顯示急遽的系統性斷裂。完整的國庫券殖利率曲線沒有呈現一致的單日壓力訊號，整體信用債工具的變動也極小。真正相關的壓力屬於結構性：直接貸款以至少8個百分點利差成交、槓桿借款人遭遇貸款人阻力，以及投資級科技債供給壓抑流通債券。市場仍然開放，但融資能力正依資金用途、讓利幅度及預期生產力分配。

## 全球存續期間、央行與財政傳導

全球利率釋放明確的政策分化訊號，並非同步寬鬆。印度央行一致決議，連續第4次會議將附買回利率維持在5.25%，並維持中性立場。印度央行總裁Sanjay Malhotra未釋出吸收流動性的訊號後，印度5年期公債殖利率下跌8個基點，10年期則下跌3個基點。市場對10月升息的定價由100%降至65%，前端出現實質重新定價，央行同時保留政策彈性。

印度按兵不動的依據，是經濟仍具韌性，且伊朗衝擊尚未全面擴散。印度央行將截至明年3月的全年通膨預測由5.1%下調至5%，GDP成長預測則由6.6%上調至6.7%。1月至3月季度成長率已達7.8%。這組數據讓官員有等待空間；但印度約90%的原油仰賴進口，通膨已升破印度央行4%目標，降雨不足也威脅食品供給。6月措施吸引逾$400億資金流入，為盧比提供緩衝，卻未消除輸入性通膨風險。

東南亞數據顯示，同樣的油價下跌可能帶來不同政策結果。菲律賓通膨由6.4%降至6.2%，低於市場原先預期的持平，主因交通通膨減緩，核心通膨也在6個月來首度放緩。披索兌美元升值0.7%至60.75。然而，米價通膨達17.1%，整體通膨仍遠高於3%目標，菲律賓央行今年也已將政策利率上調50個基點。通膨降溫可降低再次升息的急迫性，卻未創造廣泛的政策寬鬆空間。

泰國整體數據較為溫和。7月CPI由2.42%放緩至1.95%，低於市場原先預期的加速，月減0.73%。國內燃料價格是主要下跌因素，有利於央行在支撐經濟之際維持利率不變。不過，核心通膨由1.23%小幅升至1.34%，保留一項溫和的內部反向訊號。與菲律賓相比，若基礎壓力受控，能源價格下跌可驗證央行耐心等待的合理性；但當食品與匯率傳導仍然嚴重時，只能減緩升息辯論。

美日匯率協調仍是跨境影響美國公債的管道。最新細節是，美國明確表示最多可買進$100億等值日圓，並確認財政部已動用歐元部位，且持續強調Fed的外國及國際貨幣當局附買回機制（FIMA）。這些措施延續先前的干預行動，降低日本立即出售美國公債的必要性；同時也將美國政策可信度與日圓穩定連結，並承認日圓再次貶值可能擴散至亞洲貨幣。

這套支撐機制只能爭取時間，無法化解利差問題。日本持有的美國公債仍超過$1兆；在薪資穩健、最近一次10年期JGB標售需求疲弱後，日本央行的國內利率路徑仍充滿變數。FIMA可將美國公債部位轉換為美元流動性，但反覆干預仍會考驗官方資產負債表與市場信心。對美國存續期間的淨影響取決於情勢：有序支撐日圓可限制被迫賣出；干預持續或JGB殖利率上升，則可能降低日本對海外債券的需求。

中國是全球存續期間成本上升的反例。中國財政部分別發行人民幣10億元的15年期及30年期離岸人民幣債券，殖利率均創歷史新低，分別為1.99%及2.24%。各券期合計標售的投標倍數達4.67倍，是前年6月以來最高；中國境內10年期公債殖利率則已降至兩個月低點1.71%。在美國長天期殖利率仍處於歷史高檔之際，這直接證明市場對中國長存續期間債券的需求。

對美國公債而言，全球結論是需求競爭分化，並非一致性拋售。印度央行耐心等待及亞洲通膨下降，可降低區域升息需要，但受惠程度取決於各地食品、匯率與成長條件。中國能以極低殖利率順利發行長債；日本的匯率防衛則同時構成融資後盾與潛在外匯存底管理風險。各國政策分化，使市場不能假定油價下跌將同步帶動美國長存續期間債券買盤。

## 新興市場主權債、美元流動性與債務管理風險

儘管各國主權債基本面分歧，新興市場債務表現仍穩定。EMB下跌0.05%，15年期以上新興市場美元主權債指數則上漲0.30%。美元指數下跌0.25%至99.645。美元走弱與美國10年期殖利率持平，避免共同融資衝擊；但ETF小跌與長天期主權債上漲並存，顯示本交易日不宜解讀為利差全面收斂。

加彭帶來最強勁的正面債務管理進展。隨市場預期加彭可在不進行債務重整的情況下取得IMF方案，其美元債券2026年以來報酬達19.5%。IMF支持的稽核顯示，該國債務低於先前認知；政府利用由此開啟的融資窗口，透過一筆2033年到期債券私募籌得$9.2億。這筆交易有助處理短期債務及欠款；若最終稽核確認財政情勢，將改善與IMF達成協議的路徑。

但市場准入成本仍高。加彭私募債殖利率為12.65%，是今年新興市場主權發行人最高，其後殖利率降至約11.5%；這仍高於評級介於CCC+至CCC-之非洲發行人的10.7%平均值。該國債券對美國公債利差已縮至約608個基點，1月約為1,000個基點。因此，漲勢反映市場認為債務重整機率下降，且負債管理成功，並非市場融資成本低廉。

塞內加爾則呈現相反的稽核影響。稽核發現$70億先前隱匿的借款後，該國利差已擴大至1,541個基點；1月時，塞內加爾與加彭利差均約為1,000個基點。塞內加爾一面尋求重啟自2024年起暫停的IMF融資，一面持續透過國內借款履行債務。兩國起初的困境程度相同，但財政揭露以相反方向改變市場對資產負債表的預期，表現因而分歧。

兩國對比將制度可信度與共同美元因素區隔開來。美元走弱可緩解外部融資環境，卻無法抵銷隱匿負債或多邊支持停滯。據報，加彭2029年及2031年到期債券週三因獲利了結回吐部分漲幅，也限制市場直接延伸年初至今報酬率的趨勢。最終稽核、IMF條件與再融資成本，將決定改善能否持續。

中國離岸人民幣債券標售展現另一種韌性，與硬通貨邊境市場風險不同。需求強勁、長天期殖利率創歷史新低，顯示即使已開發市場實質殖利率居高，本幣主權長存續期間債券仍能吸引全球資金。加彭美元融資成本達兩位數，中國長天期人民幣債券殖利率則低於2.25%，兩者不應合併為單一新興市場訊號。貨幣制度、國內儲蓄、信用品質與發行目的的重要性，均高於共同的新興市場標籤。

因此，美元流動性只在邊際提供支撐，並非決定性因素。美元下跌、美國名目殖利率穩定，長天期新興市場主權債指數報酬為正；然而，主權債表現更大程度取決於稽核可信度、IMF融資管道、到期債務管理及本地融資替代方案。市場整體運作維持正常，但揭露改善的發行人與債務總額仍有爭議的發行人之間，資訊落差持續擴大。

## 跨資產

跨資產表現反映動能消退，並非廣泛風險反轉。標普500指數下跌0.17%，Nasdaq 100下跌0.83%，半導體指數下跌1.40%；此前科技股連續4個交易日上漲，為標普500指數創造約$3.7兆市值。半導體指數一週仍上漲14.95%。股市小幅回檔、美國10年期殖利率持平，顯示部位動能耗盡與個別公司壓力，並非足以驅動資金避險轉進美國公債的成長衝擊。

波動率支持這項解讀。即使股市下跌，VIX仍下跌4.18%至15.81，顯示投資人並未提高廣泛短期股票避險的支付價格。高收益債基金變動不到0.1%，美元也走弱。這組表現與急性融資事件不符，也說明美國公債對Fed鷹派言論的反應為何受控：風險狀況偏弱，足以避免債市再遭拋售；市場仍有序，卻未能為存續期間帶來避險買盤。

能源繼續確認近期通膨壓力緩解，但力道遠低於前一交易日。WTI降至$75.03，布蘭特原油持平於$79.36，兩者一週跌幅均超過11%。10年期損益兩平通膨率下跌1個基點，方向一致。荷姆茲海峽可能達成60天協議的報導，支撐通膨降溫管道；但胡塞組織再度威脅航運，且實際交通尚未證實恢復正常，使尾端風險仍未消除。

黃金是主要反向訊號。儘管油價持平至下跌、美國公債損益兩平通膨率下降，期貨仍在美元走弱之際大漲5.83%至$4,334.10。部分漲勢可反映美元走弱帶來的機械性支撐，但如此幅度也顯示，市場仍在防範當日通膨定價未反映的地緣政治與政策結果。金價並未否定油價訊號，而是顯示市場對協議能否持久，以及Fed長期通膨反應的信心仍不完整。

因此，跨資產檢驗的結論相當明確。油價與損益兩平通膨率下降，支持眼前能源衝擊減輕；波動率平穩、信用債基金穩定、股市僅小幅下跌，均排除系統性壓力訊號。金價上漲及股市自近期科技股漲勢轉出，使市場仍對地緣政治執行、AI估值及政策可信度保持謹慎；這與美國公債收盤時通膨補償下降、實質殖利率卻未回落的情況一致。

## 前瞻市場意義

8月7日公布的7月就業報告，將決定Fed鷹派官員的需求診斷，能否取代油價利多成為市場主軸。若非農就業增幅明顯高於預期的85,000人，尤其失業率維持在4.2%附近，且工資敏感細項強勁，Kashkari逐步升息的主張及Schmid對強勁需求的疑慮，將獲得國內數據支持。重新定價應率先出現在2年期、5年期券與較高實質殖利率。若數據疲弱，只有前端與實質殖利率同步下降，漲勢才會擴大；若仍僅損益兩平通膨率下跌，實質利率偏緊的環境將維持不變。

擬議中的60天荷姆茲海峽安排，必須實現安全通航、航運正常化及保險成本下降，能源重新定價才能持續。若美國、伊朗與阿曼簽署框架，清楚處理胡塞組織威脅，且實體航運持續暢通，油價下跌便可傳導至亞洲通膨、Fed定價及企業利潤。若協議延遲、武裝團體阻撓，或供應再度中斷，使WTI及布蘭特原油回升至談判前水準，損益兩平通膨率將重新承壓，也會凸顯目前通膨補償偏低。即使油價一週下跌，金價大漲仍顯示情勢反轉的代價不可忽視。

下週$1,250億再融資標售，將檢驗附息債券供給穩定的指引，是否足以壓抑長端溢價。若各次標售需求有序，且企業發債持續之際次級市場表現仍能守穩，將驗證美國財政部延後調整發行規模，並把當前壓力集中在國庫券及未來會計年度的決定。若標售結果疲弱，或交易商承接比例偏高，市場注意力將由安定人心的指引轉向本季$7,390億借款需求。10年至30年期曲線是敏感管道，因其殖利率一個月來的升勢，歷經油價崩跌及最新公告後仍未消退。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

The August 5 U.S. fixed-income close turned the preceding two-day rally into a holding pattern rather than a reversal. The 2-year Treasury yield fell 2 basis points to 4.18%, the 5- and 10-year yields were unchanged at 4.33% and 4.63%, and the 30-year eased 1 basis point to 5.17%. Progress toward a temporary reopening of the Strait of Hormuz continued to compress the immediate energy-inflation tail, but increasingly explicit Fed calls for higher rates and the persistence of high real yields prevented that relief from carrying the belly lower for a third session.

The composition of the close exposes the tension. The 10-year breakeven declined another 1 basis point to 2.22%, extending the inflation repricing that had accompanied the collapse in oil over the prior two sessions. The 10-year real yield rose 1 basis point to 2.41%, leaving the nominal yield unchanged. WTI fell 0.98% to $75.03 and Brent held at $79.36, even as reports advanced from a possible demining arrangement to a prospective 60-day shipping deal among the U.S., Iran and Oman. The market removed more near-term energy premium without lowering the real return required to own duration.

Fed communication supplied the principal counterforce. Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari said incremental increases should begin now, left three hikes by year-end within the range of possibility and tied the path to whether inflation remains sideways or worsens. Kansas City Fed President Jeff Schmid separately argued that strong demand and investment mean current policy is not restrictive and warned against assuming a supply-driven inflation burst will fade. Their emphasis on demand persistence matters because U.S. AI investment is estimated near $600 billion in 2026, or 1.8% of GDP, giving the economy a large investment impulse even as lower oil reduces headline pressure.

Treasury's refunding statement removed an immediate supply shock but preserved the longer-horizon financing problem. Coupon and floating-rate note sizes are expected to remain unchanged for at least several quarters, while the department replaced a reference to future issuance "increases" with the broader word "changes." The new wording allows more flexibility, yet current-quarter borrowing has already been lifted by $68 billion to $739 billion. Stable near-term coupons helped keep the 30-year from selling off, but dependence on bills and the absence of a durable answer to rising borrowing needs kept term relief shallow.

Credit and global markets reinforced a regime of functioning absorption with pronounced dispersion. U.S. credit funds were almost unchanged, a $2.2 billion private loan for a health-care acquisition was progressing at a spread of at least 8 percentage points, and heavy hyperscaler issuance continued to pressure technology bonds. Abroad, the RBI held at 5.25% and sharply reduced market expectations for an October increase, while Philippine inflation remained 6.2% and Thailand's slowed to 1.95%. Gabon's improving IMF prospects contrasted with Senegal's debt distress. The common energy shock is fading, but policy space and financing terms remain determined by local inflation, fiscal credibility and capital structure.

## UST Rates, Fed Pricing, Real Yields, And Curve Structure

The Treasury curve registered modest front-end relief and little movement elsewhere. The 2-year's 2-basis-point decline exceeded the 1-basis-point fall in the 30-year, while the 5- and 10-year points were unchanged. The 2s10s slope widened 2 basis points to 45 and 2s30s steepened 1 basis point to 99. This was a small bull steepening driven by the policy-sensitive tenor, not a broad duration rally. It follows a session in which the 5- and 10-year sectors had led a larger decline in yields, leaving the current close as consolidation around those lower levels.

The weekly comparison shows that the relief has been meaningful but incomplete. The 2-, 5- and 10-year yields were each 4 basis points lower over 1 week, and the 30-year was 3 basis points lower. Over 1 month, however, the curve remained 4 basis points higher at 2 years, 10 at 5 years, 14 at 10 years and 19 at 30 years. The oil reversal has repaired the latest weekly shock, while the larger monthly increase toward the long end still prices elevated real returns, policy uncertainty and fiscal supply.

Inflation-linked pricing separates those horizons. The 10-year real yield rose to 2.41% as the breakeven slipped to 2.22%, producing no change in the nominal 10-year yield. At 2.96%, the 30-year real yield was unchanged on the day and remained 17 basis points higher over 1 month. The latest nominal stability therefore masks a further transfer from expected inflation into real discount rates. Lower energy prices reduced the probability of an immediate second-round shock, but did not persuade investors that the Fed's reaction function or the long-run return on capital had become less demanding.

That split also complicates the argument that low breakevens settle the inflation question. Barclays and HSBC strategists highlighted long-dated inflation-linked debt as protection against delayed Fed action, at a time when breakevens were near a one-year low and 30-year real yields had recently reached their highest since 2008. Their concern is forward-looking and does not override the day's lower inflation compensation. It identifies the asymmetry: the market can price immediate Hormuz relief while still assigning value to protection against a reversal in energy or a policy response that permits inflation persistence.

Kashkari made the near-term policy challenge more explicit than in the prior close. He called for rates to begin moving up incrementally, while remaining uncertain about the September decision and conditioning further action on incoming data. His statement that three increases by year-end are possible broadens the distribution around the path without supplying a probability. Schmid's argument reaches beyond energy, locating the need for tighter policy in strong demand and investment and warning that supply shocks become more inflationary when demand is firm.

The AI investment impulse gives that demand argument quantitative weight. Estimated global AI capital spending of about $1 trillion in 2026 includes just under $600 billion in the U.S. The U.S. share is projected at 1.8% of GDP this year, rising to 2.5% in 2027 and 2.8% in 2028. Those estimates are not a same-session activity release, but they show why a lower oil path need not produce an equally large decline in real yields. Investment can sustain growth, financing demand and resource pressure even when the external inflation impulse moderates.

Debt management offered immediate reassurance on auction sizes. Treasury retained guidance that nominal coupons and floating-rate notes will remain unchanged for at least several quarters, consistent with expectations that changes would be pushed well into 2027. Next week's $125 billion refunding is expected to raise about $28.7 billion of new cash. The announcement establishes the calendar and near-term quantity; demand quality will depend on the auctions themselves.

The subtle wording change preserves a separate term-premium issue. Treasury now says it is evaluating future "changes" rather than "increases" in coupon and floating-rate note sales, while retaining a bias toward the shorter end for any eventual increase. TBAC said current projections could still warrant higher coupon issuance in the fiscal year beginning October 1 and urged language that preserves flexibility. Against a $739 billion quarterly borrowing estimate, unchanged coupons shift more financing toward bills and increase sensitivity to future short-rate shocks rather than eliminating the funding requirement.

The rates conclusion is a stable nominal close produced by opposing forces. Hormuz progress and lower oil continued to reduce inflation compensation and allowed the 2-year to rally. Hawkish Fed communication, strong investment demand and unresolved future borrowing kept real yields elevated and the belly unchanged. The weekly selloff has been reversed; the month-long rise in the long end has not, leaving the curve dependent on realized domestic data and actual auction absorption.

## Credit, Funding, And Primary-Market Absorption

Broad U.S. credit prices were quiet around the flat Treasury close. LQD fell 0.02%, HYG declined 0.04% and JNK lost 0.08%. The moves were too small to indicate a broad repricing of credit risk, and the fund returns do not identify cash-spread direction. Longer corporate bond indices gained about 0.16% on the date, close to the 0.20% rise in the 20-year-plus Treasury index. Aggregate duration remained functional while issuer-specific financing terms carried the more useful information.

Private credit demonstrated capacity for a large acquisition financing, at a high clearing cost. Ares Management was leading a $2.2 billion direct loan supporting MedImpact Holdings' planned purchase of Puerto Rico-based Medical Card System. The loan could pay at least 8 percentage points over its benchmark. Completion on those terms would show that the market can absorb a large health-care transaction after record redemptions disrupted the sector, but the spread embeds substantial compensation for leverage, illiquidity and execution risk.

The transaction sits between the extremes visible in the preceding close. It lacks the enormous orderbook and investment-grade curve access achieved by AbbVie, but it is also progressing where Baker Tilly's syndicated package failed after lenders demanded more spread for a refinancing tied to a sponsor dividend. The current delta is renewed private-market capacity for acquisition financing when economics are sufficiently generous. Use of proceeds and lender compensation remain more decisive than a 1- or 2-basis-point change in Treasuries.

Hyperscaler debt presents a broader portfolio-absorption problem. U.S. investment-grade markets have carried a disproportionate share of financing for AI infrastructure, and existing bonds have weakened as investors make room for new supply and question the returns on capital spending. Amazon's $25 billion sale last month prompted selling in outstanding hyperscaler paper to fund primary purchases. In July, average spreads widened about 22 basis points for Meta and 29 basis points for Oracle, showing direct pressure within the sector rather than a generic duration effect.

European markets are becoming part of the same supply channel. Alphabet has issued debut sterling and Swiss-franc bonds as well as euro debt, and further diversification by large technology borrowers could erode the relative valuation advantage of European investment grade. Strong balance sheets limit immediate solvency concern for many issuers; the unresolved issue is whether investment proceeds earn enough to justify sustained borrowing. Large supply can weaken secondary performance even when every borrower retains access and defaults remain remote.

This mechanism links macro resilience to credit pressure. AI investment supports U.S. demand and helps keep real yields high, yet financing that investment forces corporate portfolios to create capacity and increases concentration in a single capital-spending theme. Income may offset part of the mark-to-market drag, but repeated primary concessions or selling of seasoned bonds would reveal a declining marginal appetite. The distinction is between available money and the price at which portfolios will accept another round of technology duration.

Funding conditions did not show an acute systemic break. The complete bill curve offered no coherent same-day stress signal, and broad credit vehicles barely moved. The relevant strains were instead structural: a direct loan clearing at a spread of at least 8 percentage points, leveraged borrowers facing lender resistance, and investment-grade technology supply pressuring outstanding bonds. Markets remain open, but financing capacity is being allocated according to purpose, concession and expected productivity.

## Global Duration, Central Banks, And Fiscal Transmission

Global rates delivered a clear policy-dispersion signal rather than synchronized easing. The RBI unanimously kept the repo rate at 5.25% for a fourth meeting and retained a neutral stance. Five-year Indian government yields fell 8 basis points, compared with a 3-basis-point decline in the 10-year, after Governor Sanjay Malhotra offered no signal of liquidity absorption. Market pricing for an October increase dropped to 65% from 100%, a material repricing of the front end even as the central bank preserved optionality.

India's hold rests on resilience and a judgment that the Iran shock has not generalized. The RBI lowered its inflation forecast for the year through March to 5% from 5.1% and raised its GDP forecast to 6.7% from 6.6%. Growth had reached 7.8% in the January-March quarter. That combination gives officials room to wait, although India imports roughly 90% of its crude, inflation has moved above the RBI's 4% target, and deficient rainfall threatens food supply. More than $40 billion of inflows attracted by June measures cushions the rupee without removing imported-inflation risk.

Southeast Asian releases showed why a common decline in oil creates different policy outcomes. Philippine inflation slowed to 6.2% from 6.4%, below expectations for no change, as transport inflation eased and core inflation decelerated for the first time in six months. The peso strengthened 0.7% to 60.75 per dollar. Yet rice inflation was 17.1%, headline inflation remained far above the 3% target, and the BSP had already raised its key rate by 50 basis points this year. Slower inflation reduces the urgency of another move without creating broad policy relief.

Thailand's data were more benign at the headline level. July CPI slowed to 1.95% from 2.42%, below expectations for an acceleration, and fell 0.73% on the month. Domestic fuel prices drove much of the decline, supporting the central bank's decision to hold as it supports the economy. Core inflation edged up to 1.34% from 1.23%, however, preserving a small internal counter-signal. The contrast with the Philippines shows that cheaper energy can validate patience where underlying pressure is contained, but only slow a tightening debate where food and currency pass-through remain severe.

U.S.-Japanese currency coordination remains a cross-border Treasury channel. The latest detail was an explicit signal that the U.S. could buy as much as $10 billion of yen, together with confirmation that Treasury had used euro holdings and continued to highlight the Fed's FIMA repo facility. These steps extend the earlier intervention campaign by reducing the need for Japan to liquidate Treasuries immediately. They also attach U.S. policy credibility to yen stability and acknowledge that renewed depreciation could spread across Asian currencies.

The support mechanism buys time rather than resolving the rate differential. Japan still holds more than $1 trillion of Treasuries, and the BOJ's domestic rate path remains live after firm wages and weak demand at the latest 10-year JGB auction. FIMA can transform Treasury holdings into dollar liquidity, but repeated intervention would still test official balance sheets and market confidence. The net effect on U.S. duration is conditional: orderly yen support limits forced sales, whereas persistent operations or higher JGB yields can reduce Japan's appetite for foreign bonds.

China offered a counterexample to rising global duration costs. The Ministry of Finance sold CNY1 billion each of 15- and 30-year offshore yuan bonds at record-low yields of 1.99% and 2.24%. The combined auction across maturities drew a 4.67 bid-to-cover ratio, the strongest since June of the prior year, while China's onshore 10-year yield had fallen to a two-month low of 1.71%. This is direct evidence of demand for Chinese duration at a time when U.S. long yields remain historically elevated.

For Treasuries, the global conclusion is mixed competition rather than a common selloff. RBI patience and lower Asian inflation can reduce the need for regional tightening, yet the benefits depend on domestic food, currency and growth conditions. China can clear long bonds at exceptionally low yields, while Japan's currency defense creates both a funding backstop and a potential reserve-management risk. Foreign policy dispersion limits any assumption that lower oil will generate a synchronized bid for U.S. duration.

## EM Sovereigns, Dollar Liquidity, And Debt-Management Risk

Emerging-market debt was stable despite divergent underlying sovereign stories. EMB slipped 0.05%, while the 15-year-plus EM dollar sovereign bond index gained 0.30%. The Dollar Index fell 0.25% to 99.645. Softer dollar conditions and a flat U.S. 10-year prevented a common funding shock, but the split between a small ETF decline and a gain in long sovereign duration argues against treating the session as uniform spread compression.

Gabon supplied the strongest positive debt-management update. Its dollar bonds had returned 19.5% in 2026 as expectations grew that an IMF program could be reached without restructuring. An IMF-supported audit indicated lower debt than previously understood, and the government used the resulting window to raise $920 million privately through a bond due in 2033. The transaction helps address short-term obligations and arrears, improving the path toward an IMF agreement if the final audit confirms the fiscal picture.

Access remained expensive. Gabon's private placement yielded 12.65%, the highest for an emerging sovereign this year, before its yield declined to about 11.5%. That still exceeded the 10.7% average for African issuers rated from CCC+ to CCC-. Its spread over Treasuries had narrowed to about 608 basis points, compared with roughly 1,000 in January. The rally therefore reflects a lower perceived probability of restructuring and successful liability management, not inexpensive market access.

Senegal shows the opposite audit channel. Its spread had widened to 1,541 basis points after an audit uncovered $7 billion of previously hidden borrowing, compared with the roughly 1,000-basis-point level shared by both Senegal and Gabon in January. Senegal has continued meeting obligations through domestic borrowing while seeking to revive an IMF facility suspended since 2024. Identical starting distress levels have diverged because fiscal disclosure changed the expected balance sheet in opposite directions.

The comparison isolates institutional credibility from the common dollar factor. A weaker dollar can ease the external financing environment, but it cannot compensate for hidden liabilities or stalled multilateral support. Gabon's 2029 and 2031 bonds gave back part of their rally on Wednesday, reportedly on profit-taking, which also limits extrapolation from the year-to-date return. The final audit, IMF terms and the cost of refinancing will determine whether the improvement becomes durable.

China's offshore yuan auction demonstrates another form of resilience, distinct from hard-currency frontier risk. Strong demand and record-low long yields show that local-currency sovereign duration can attract global capital even as developed-market real yields remain high. Gabon's double-digit dollar cost and China's sub-2.25% long-yuan yields should not be collapsed into a single EM signal. Currency regime, domestic savings, credit quality and the purpose of issuance dominate the shared label.

Dollar liquidity was therefore supportive at the margin, not decisive. The dollar declined, U.S. nominal yields were stable and long EM sovereign index returns were positive. Sovereign outcomes were governed more powerfully by audit credibility, IMF access, maturity management and local funding alternatives. The session preserved broad market function while widening the informational gap between issuers with improving disclosure and those whose debt stock remains contested.

## Cross asset

Cross assets describe fading momentum rather than a broad risk reversal. The S&P 500 slipped 0.17%, the Nasdaq 100 fell 0.83% and the semiconductor index declined 1.40% after a four-session technology rally had created roughly $3.7 trillion of S&P 500 value. The semiconductor index was still 14.95% higher over 1 week. A modest equity pullback alongside a flat 10-year yield suggests position exhaustion and company-specific pressure, not a growth shock large enough to drive a flight into Treasuries.

Volatility supports that reading. The VIX fell 4.18% to 15.81 even as equities declined, indicating that investors did not pay more for broad near-term equity protection. High-yield credit funds moved by less than 0.1%, and the dollar weakened. The combination is inconsistent with an acute funding event. It also explains why the Treasury response to hawkish Fed remarks remained contained: risk conditions were soft enough to avoid a renewed selloff, but orderly enough to deny duration a haven bid.

Energy continued to confirm near-term inflation relief, though with much less force than in the preceding close. WTI declined to $75.03 while Brent held at $79.36, leaving both more than 11% lower over 1 week. The 10-year breakeven's 1-basis-point fall matched that direction. Reports of a possible 60-day Hormuz arrangement supported the disinflation channel, while a renewed Houthi threat to shipping and the absence of demonstrated traffic normalization kept the tail open.

Gold was the principal contradiction. Futures surged 5.83% to $4,334.10 as the dollar fell, even though oil was stable to lower and Treasury breakevens declined. Part of the move can reflect the mechanical support from a softer dollar, but its scale also indicates demand for protection against geopolitical and policy outcomes not captured by the day's inflation pricing. Gold does not negate the oil signal; it shows that confidence in a durable settlement and in the Fed's longer-run inflation response remains incomplete.

The cross-asset check is consequently narrow. Lower oil and breakevens support relief from the immediate energy shock. Calm volatility, stable credit funds and only modest equity losses reject systemic stress. Gold and the equity rotation away from the recent technology surge preserve caution around geopolitical execution, AI valuations and policy credibility, matching a Treasury close in which inflation compensation fell but real yields did not.

## Forward Market Significance

The July employment report on August 7 determines whether the Fed hawks' demand diagnosis can displace the oil-relief narrative. Payroll growth materially above the expected 85,000 pace, especially with unemployment holding near 4.2% and firm wage-sensitive detail, would give Kashkari's incremental-hike case and Schmid's concern about strong demand a domestic foundation. Repricing should appear first in the 2- and 5-year sectors and in higher real yields. A weaker report would deepen the rally only if real yields fall with the front end; another decline confined to breakevens would leave the restrictive real-rate regime intact.

The proposed 60-day Hormuz arrangement must produce secure passage, normalized shipping and lower insurance costs before the energy repricing becomes durable. A signed U.S.-Iran-Oman framework, clear treatment of Houthi threats and sustained physical traffic would allow lower crude to feed through Asian inflation, Fed pricing and corporate margins. Delay, obstruction by armed groups or renewed disruption that lifts WTI and Brent back toward pre-negotiation levels would reopen breakeven pressure and expose the market's low inflation compensation. Gold's surge shows that the cost of that reversal remains relevant even after oil's weekly decline.

Next week's $125 billion refunding auctions determine whether stable coupon guidance is sufficient to contain the long-end premium. Orderly demand at the stated sales, followed by secondary performance that holds as corporate issuance continues, would validate Treasury's decision to defer size changes and keep the current pressure concentrated in bills and future fiscal years. Weak auction outcomes or heavy dealer absorption would shift attention from the reassuring guidance to the $739 billion quarterly borrowing need. The 10- to 30-year curve is the sensitive channel because the monthly rise in yields survived both the oil collapse and the latest announcement.
